text: A frequency study answers one question.
Can a new radio site use this channel without interfering with anyone licensed nearby?
It finds every nearby licensee, draws their protected areas and the new site's reach, and checks the overlaps.
A project is thousands of these: every site, times every channel.
On one project of 7,630 studies, the web tool it replaced needed 96 minutes.
say: On one project of seven thousand six hundred and thirty studies, the web tool it replaced needed ninety-six minutes.

text: I rebuilt how studies run, with one rule: every answer must match the old tool.
Studies now wait in a queue inside the database.
Each worker claims one and holds a lease, so any machine can join in.
One shared worker pool replaced a pool per group.
Searching a state's border for licensees took 26.6 seconds.
say: Searching a state's border for licensees took twenty-six point six seconds.

text: Cut into small pieces, the border takes a third of a second.
A cloud database would have turned a ten-minute run into days, so the engine stays next to its data.
The same 7,630 studies now finish in under three minutes.
say: The same seven thousand six hundred and thirty studies now finish in under three minutes.

text: That's 33 times faster, with the same answers.
say: That's thirty-three times faster, with the same answers.

text: In production, one 96-core server ran 151,214 studies in about 40 minutes.
say: In production, one ninety-six core server ran a hundred and fifty-one thousand, two hundred and fourteen studies in about forty minutes.
